While it is widely accepted that the Draugr appeared sometime during the Sanjak Revolution, little is known of its origins beyond that. Some point to reports made by the KTS early in the conflict where soldiers described encountering a specialized Vlad shrouded in fog. Others question whether certain Hecatoncheires sightings were in fact Draugrs due to inordinate Karrakin losses. From rumors of possessed Balors to blurry photos of upscaled Kobolds, the mystery surrounding the Draugr’s history makes it a hotspot for speculation across the omninet.
One curious fact, however, is that deep within the Draugr pattern's metadata, buried in liturgicode and empty files, is a number: 4600.

DISASTER INVESTIGATION REPORT: Cabalia-A-03(L6-G3-S2-W2)
LOCATION: Himalaya-Annapurna, Agni-Cabalia1
DATE: 08-5015u
CLASS: MAG-8, Anthropogenic, Paracausal

Following a disaster on the core world of Cabalia, a joint USB-DOJ/HR investigation report was provided to members of CentComm. It compiled CAM reports, local responder accounts, disaster relief reports. A second report was filed later, linking the events to the rumored Erinyes frame.

ADDENDUM, ERINYES
The Erinyes Pattern group's first appearance correlates with the disaster at Cabalia 3, the research facility run by SSC's Foreign Bodies Department at the event's center. The facility was responsible for pushing the boundaries of SSC's FCA-compliant machine learning programs. Though the specific research and methods were highly confidential, current information suggests the facility focused on neural links, Intelligence Bridging, and pilot-insight systems. The facility was also a well-known matriculation center for admittance to the Constellar Worlds. Individuals with notable experience and genetics would be brought to Cabalia 3 to assist in research before being redistributed to a fitting Constellar world. Cabalia 3 was the last point of contact before individuals disappeared into SSC's self-managed bureaucracy.

In 5015u, Cabalia 3 was subject to a paracausal event that resulted in the death or disappearance of all present personnel. Constellar Security were the first responders on sight, followed by CAM-LTs and USB investigators. Evidence discovered on site failed to reveal the event's cause, implying a paracausal source, though USB reports indicate a frustration with Constellar Security's handling of materials during the investigation. Field teams discovered that the facility and recoverable bodies bore heavy laceration and burn marks, with one report describing sections of reinforced concrete as having “melted like wax.” Surviving computer systems surrounding the facility contained unidentified files, which have since been linked to the Erinyes.

The Erinyes Pattern group started appearing in SSC-associated conflicts shortly after the events of Cabalia 3. The machine's small size, maneuverability, and painful weaponry have given it a reputation among Constellar forces and their detractors as a predator of predators. The unique pattern of lacerated burn marks left on flesh and metal make its work easy to identify, and appears to cause paranoia among those who believe themselves targeted.

SSC maintains an open bounty on the destruction or retrieval of any Erinyes models.

The Church of the Deeptide, or just The Deeptide, is a decentralized, clandestine group of sympathetic Aun who argue for the liberation of Aun'Yaa, the lunar prison home of the Apollonian people. For most, the name is a tongue-in-cheek title to reflect the group's contrarian stance against the Ascendancy. Apollonians, however, view it differently. Their ancestral mythos of angels and demons has long spawned sects and myths, and one such story, the Rite of Deeprise, tells of a demon raised up to the firmament, from which it touched realspace.
Due to its seclusion in Aunic space, the Kraken remains poorly understood. Supposedly created on the surface on Aun'Yaa, rumors claim that a powerful Mind not yet cultivated by the Ascendancy assembled a simple machine from spare parts. This Apollonian, in lieu of realspace computers, reached into the firmament for an alternative. As the half-machine took form, black tendrils of liquid shadow stretched and pulled at steel like sinew on bone. When manquellers were sent, they bore witness to an ink-dark creation of man and metal: Ofanim'Ist, the Kraken. For days it scoured the moon's surface of Aunic forces, sending survivors home defeated and blind.
It is unclear how the Kraken's story ended. Some say it was banished by Os, a proud triumph and proof of the danger unchecked Apollonians pose. Others claim it retreated to the firmament, waiting to pull unsuspecting souls into the Deep. In either case, the Kraken, and the secrets it held, vanished without a trace from the prison moon.

“World-death is always imagined to be so grand. Tomb-worlds are a treasure, after all. Full of mystery and wealth just waiting to be discovered. Researched. Plundered.
“But reality often disappoints. For every violent apocalypse, for every stellar disaster, there are a dozen slow, agonizing, and worst of all, chosen world-deaths.
“For some worlds, it comes from ignorance. From a desire to grow and learn that outstrips the discovery of consequence. It is what almost killed you, once.
“Worse than that is when itls done from malice. From a hate so vile the consequences cease to matter. You know this. You've done it.
“But the worst of all is indifference. When world-death is nothing more than a byproduct. You do it now, here, on the morning shores you covet.
“The noble vulture eats what must be eaten, removes the festering carrion that ruins what is good. This carcass you make is not yet dead, and it shall eat what must be eaten.”

Instead of changing an attacks tangibility, you can use tears to change an attack’s trajectory. When attacking with a kinetic weapon, draw range and line of sight from yourself to a tear, and the remaining range and line of sight from the tear to your target. The combined distance must be within the weapon’s range.
Line attacks can be broken into two segments this way, drawing the first segment to the tear, and the second from the tear itself. Characters hit by the second segment take half damage on a hit. The combined length of both lines must be equal to the line’s normal length.
When you check for INVISIBILITY, you may reroll the result.

Described as a lament for the dead, “keening” is a funeral call of mourning practiced by various cultures around Union space. The Banshee, though seldom seen, is always associated with a loud drone most frequently described as harsh wind or constant scream.
Note: Could the sound be related to Aunic Souls? A byproduct perhaps?
Though never recorded, some survivor accounts describe words being heard behind the howl. These included the names of present pilots, notable actions taken by present pilots, and the names of present pilot’s family members.
The earliest report possibly attributable to the Banshee is from 5010u, after Fansipan, when a rumor of “dead Ofanim” appearing from thin air circulated online.
Note: Validity is vague, but core details are consistent with later confirmed encounters.
Those who survive these encounters always note hearing the call, though other evidence implies that typically at least one combatant does not hear it.
Note: My assistant questioned if the Banshee leaves survivors on purpose. A question for another day, I think.
– Dr. Lichen, UIB Boundary Garde

Create a void tear in a free space within SENSORS. Tears are undamageable Size 1 objects that do not cause obstruction. They are visible to both tangible and INTANGIBLE characters, and act as a window between tangible and intangible space.
Intangible characters can draw line of sight to tangible targets if the line passes through a tear. Terrain and tangible objects do not exist in intangible space, and so do not block line of sight before passing through a tear.
Tangible characters can draw line of sight to Intangible characters if the line passes through a tear. Terrain and tangible objects do not block line of sight after passing through the tear.
Attacks that pass through a tear treat targets as INVISIBLE. An attack cannot travel more than half its maximum range after passing through a tear. 
You may expend your base movement to move the tear up to your speed. This does not count as taking an action. You can close the tear as a quick action.

After hitting a target with a ranged attack, you may activate your core to teleport to a space adjacent to the target, become tangible, and deal 4 AP KINETIC to the target, or 6 if the attack critically hit. You may do so even while IMMOBILIZED.
If this damage destroys the target, they leave behind no wreckage, you become INTANGIBLE, and you may move a void tear anywhere within SENSORS. 1/scene after destroying a target this way, regain your core point.
